subject: Production slowdown after recent model canary — high p95/p99 latency
messages:
From: Asha Rao <asha@brightbound.com>
To: connor.obrien@redwood.com
Cc: sre@brightbound.com
Date: 2026-06-12T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Production slowdown after recent model canary — p95/p99 spikes

Connor —

We started seeing sharp latency regressions around 08:45 PDT after you flipped the canary to model v2.1 for 10% of traffic. p95 went from ~280ms to ~1.2s and p99 has spiked to ~2.6s. This is impacting our search ranking API (heavy tail) and causing timeouts in our frontend. We've attached a small CSV of sampled latencies and our edge request ids.

Immediate asks: can you please revert the canary to v2.0 for BrightBound traffic and confirm? Also we need logs from the inference nodes and any config changes you pushed in the last hour.

We are looped in on this thread: BrightBound SRE (sre@brightbound.com). This is high-impact for our traffic profile — tagging for urgency.

Thanks,
Asha Rao
Head of Infrastructure, BrightBound

Taking point. I'm looking at the autoscaling traces and model runtime telemetry now. Preliminary signal: v2.1 increases KV-cache pressure for longer prompt prefixes and seems to trigger a higher variance in token latency for long-context requests.

Action items I'm executing:
- Rolling the BrightBound canary back to v2.0 (should complete in ~3 minutes).
- Capturing full trace logs from the affected inference pool and exporting to support_log_0612.zip (attaching once ready).
- Pinning the legacy kernel/profile for their model variant until we fully analyze.

Connor — I'll post when rollback completes. Marissa/Hannah please prep a short customer note once we confirm rollback and stability.

-David
David Kim
Director, Serving Runtime, Redwood Inference

Attached: p99_trend_0612.png (5min buckets) and the raw latency sample CSV. I'll follow with the full logs.

Also we need the exact time window and request ids for forensic logs that our security team asked for — can you provide those?

Asha
From: marissa_cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: asha@brightbound.com, connor.obrien@redwood.com, david_kim@redwood.com, hannah_schmitt@redwood.com
Date: 2026-06-12T11:18:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Production slowdown after recent model canary — p95/p99 spikes

Asha — really sorry about the disruption and thanks for flagging quickly. Quick summary for your teams:
- What happened: Canary rollout of model v2.1 introduced a kernel-level execution path that increases path variability for requests with >1k tokens of context under your workload. That variability surfaced as heavy tail latency at p95/p99 for some request shapes.
- Immediate action we took: Rolled BrightBound traffic back to v2.0 at 09:36 PDT; verified early stability. Provided sample traces and logs to your SRE.
- Next steps and ETA: Engineering is doing a targeted repro and will deliver a patch that either disables the new kernel optimization for affected contexts or falls back to cached KV behavior. Initial ETA for a safe, tested release is 5 business days; we'll escalate if repro accelerates it.

Hannah will coordinate a postmortem and timeline for a follow-up call with your engineering/security teams. Connor will follow on commercial impacts and credit requests if needed.

Marissa Cole
VP, Customer Success, Redwood Inference
From: hannah_schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.com>
To: Asha Rao <asha@brightbound.com>, connor_obrien@redwood.com, marissa_cole@redwood.com, david_kim@redwood.com

Subject: Re: Production slowdown after recent model canary — p95/p99 spikes

1) Schedule a 30-minute alignment call with BrightBound SRE + Redwood runtime engineers today or tomorrow to walk through logs and confirm the repro. Proposed times: 16:30 PDT today or 10:00 PDT tomorrow. Please reply with availability.
2) We'll open an INF ticket for the fix (INF-2247) and share daily status updates until resolved.
3) Connor will file the commercial request if BrightBound requests a service credit for the incident window (09:36–09:50 PDT).

Attached I've added the Grafana dashboard link for your team and the exported logs.

Hannah Schmitt
